title: Burglary: Intent of Aider and Abettor

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: To be guilty of burglary as an aider and abettor, the defendant must have known of the perpetrator’s unlawful purpose and must have formed the intent to aid, facilitate, promote, instigate, or encourage commission of the burglary before the perpetrator finally left the structure.

bench_notes.text: The court has a sua sponte duty to give this instruction when the defendant is charged with aiding and abetting a burglary and there is an issue about when the defendant allegedly formed the intent to aid and abet.
This instruction must be given with CALCRIM No. 401, *Aiding and Abetting: Intended Crimes*.
Do not give this instruction if the defendant is charged with felony murder.

authority.text: • Aider and Abettor to Burglary—When Intent Formed. *People v. Montoya* (1994) 7 Cal.4th 1027, 1044–1046 [31 Cal.Rptr.2d 128, 874 P.2d 903].
